item.title: [Representative figure added] Twinned-magnesium metal negative electrodes enable reversible magnesium electrodeposition
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Disentangling the effect of space and electric field on photoelectrochemical water splitting
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77786-5

Photoelectrochemical performance strongly depends on charge separation within space charge layer, but the precise mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors disentangle the effect of space charge layer width and built-in electric field on charge dynamics using in-situ time-resolved techniques.

item.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Spiroannulation to Access Polycyclic Spiro Enones via Transient Axial-to-Point Chirality Induction and Transfer
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77436-w

Chiral polycyclic spirocycles are privileged molecular scaffolds for drug discovery and asymmetric synthesis, yet their efficient stereoselective construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report a Pd/Sadphos-catalyzed asymmetric dearomative cascade that delivers polycyclic spiro enones with three contiguous stereocenters and exceptional stereoselectivity.

item.title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77557-2

Protein language models are powerful tools for generative protein design, but because they are trained solely on natural sequences, they often struggle to generate proteins with enhanced or non-natural functions. This work a general framework that aligns generative protein language models with experimentally defined functional objectives.

item.title: CG14075/Mmt promotes amino acid catabolism and cooperates with AKH during starvation in Drosophila
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77687-7

How animals survive without food depends on more than stored fat and sugar. This study shows that the fruit fly hormone CG14075/Marmite helps redirect amino acid use during starvation, working with a key hormone, AKH, to sustain energy balance.

item.title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76876-8

Oxytocin receptor signaling in the nucleus accumbens supports pair bonding, but its role in attachment-related neural activity is unclear. Here, the authors show that Oxtr loss sex-specifically alters pair bonding and nucleus accumbens activity in prairie voles; in males, early activity predicts partner preference.

item.title: Widespread declines of formerly common species reshape local assemblages over time
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77501-4

Human-driven environmental change is reshaping ecological communities worldwide. Analysing 4,748 sites across 129 studies, we show that formerly common species decline disproportionately compared to rare species in marine and terrestrial assemblages.

item.title: Reprogramming the Rossmann fold signature motif creates orthogonal redox biocatalysts
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77633-7

Developing NMN⁺ as an orthogonal redox cofactor could help biomanufacturing approach theoretical maximum yields. Here, the authors show that engineering the Rossmann fold can convert NAD(P)-dependent enzymes to selectively use the noncanonical cofactor NMN(H).

item.title: A single-nucleus atlas of ligular region uncovers brassinosteroid-driven cell fate transitions controlling leaf angle in maize
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77393-4

Here the authors integrate single-nucleus transcriptomic and cellular analyse to reveal that brassinosteroid drives cell division, elongation, and subsequent lignification in the ligular region, thereby controlling leaf angle diversity in maize.

item.title: Two-dimensional metal oxide polaritonics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77629-3

Metal oxides support a broad range of polaritons. In this review, the authors extend this to the emerging family of two-dimensional metal oxides and cover the impact of crystal structure and extrinsic manipulation on the polaritons along with synthesis approaches and future photonics applications.

item.title: Leveraging high-throughput proteomics and AI-based protein folding to accelerate VAV1 molecular glue discovery
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77657-z

VAV1 is a blood-cell signaling protein linked to leukemia and autoimmune disease. Here, the authors discover CRBN molecular glues that degrade VAV1 via a non-canonical degron, using proteomics and AI-based structural modeling to guide the design of more potent degraders.

item.title: Efficient conversion of syngas into sustainable aviation fuel
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77708-5

Fischer−Tropsch synthesis to paraffinic kerosene is a crucial pathway to obtain sustainable aviation fuel, but a more efficient catalyst is needed for practical applications. Here, the authors report a cobalt manganese catalyst supported on tetrapropylammonium hydroxide-etched Beta zeolites that addresses the long-standing activity-selectivity trade-off.

item.title: Proteasome inhibition alleviates proteinuria in Lmx1b knock-in mice with dysfunctional LIM domains
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77485-1

Mutations in the LIM domains of LMX1B cause ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and result in podocyte injury. Inhibition of the proteasome ameliorated renal symptoms in Lmx1b knock-in mice, thus providing proof of principle for a novel therapeutic strategy.

item.title: A neural circuit of food sight-promoted feeding and contextual memory in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77682-y

Feeding can be regulated by sensory cues. This study identifies a multi-layer circuit that mediates food sight-promoted feeding and food-related memory in mice.

item.title: CReP-mediated control of eIF2α phosphorylation is a critical node in MYC-driven medulloblastoma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77565-2

Group 3 (G3) medulloblastoma is an aggressive paediatric brain tumour with limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that CReP phosphatase maintains eIF2α activity, thereby protecting G3 MB cells from apoptosis, and that these cells are sensitive to eIF2α inactivation.

item.title: Chronic loneliness and isolation phenotypes and physical and mental health in older adults
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77683-x

Chronic loneliness was associated with poorer physical and mental health, while loneliness onset showed similar but weaker associations. Social isolation primarily affected mental health, while remission may confer cognitive benefits.

item.title: SLC4A7/NBCn1 maintains intracellular pH to support mTORC1 activity and antibody-secreting cell differentiation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77588-9

Environmental cues, such as pH, determine cellular differentiation and function, including that of immune cells. Here the authors identify SLC4A7, a Na + /HCO3–cotransporter as a critical and specific regulator of plasmablast differentiation genetic deletion of which in mice impairing antibody responses.

item.title: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77680-0

Preterm birth poses severe risks to mothers and newborns. Here, the authors identify an oxytocin receptor antagonist nanobody with tocolytic effects in mice, offering a potential roadmap for developing next generation tocolytic drugs.

item.title: Predictability can be dynamically constructed in deterministic systems
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77737-0

In a deterministic, non-chaotic system, the initial state fixes the future completely, yet that future may be impossible to forecast from it. Using a cellular automaton of communicating cells, this study shows that predictability is instead built by the dynamics: collective topological structures self-organize as the system evolves, and only once they exist does the eventual outcome become legible.

item.title: Structural basis of IgLON5 autoantibody recognition in autoimmune encephalitis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77812-6

Anti-IgLON5 disease is a rare neuro-immunological disorder characterized by the production of autoantibodies against the cell adhesion molecule, IgLON5. Here, the authors examine the B cell receptor repertoire of an individual with this condition and present a cryo–electron microscopy structure of a patient-derived antibody clone in complex with IgLON5.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Periodic polar vortices in BaTiO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> superlattices monolithically grown on silicon
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Himito: a graph-based toolkit for mitochondrial genome analysis using long reads
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77418-y

Himito is a graph-based toolkit for long-read mitochondrial genome analysis. It integrates NUMT filtering, haplotype assembly, variant calling, and methylation profiling, providing a comprehensive framework for studying mtDNA in aging and human disease.

item.title: Site-specific protein functionalization by late-stage reversible cysteine masking
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77718-3

Site-selective functionalization strategies are essential for generating complex proteins for basic research and biomedical applications, but achieving precise transformations across protein sequences remains challenging. Here, the authors report a modular strategy for site-selective protein functionalization that enables the selective targeting of desired cysteine residues through late-stage reversible thiol caging (ReCag).

item.title: Additive-assisted quasi-dry process enabling freestanding sulfide electrolyte films for all-solid-state batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77590-1

Thin sulfide electrolyte film could raise energy density of solid state battery, but producing thin, highly conductive film remains difficult. Here, authors develop an α-pinene assisted quasi-dry process to improve film quality and demonstrate a pouch cell retaining 83% capacity after 1000 cycles.

item.title: Placental TRPV2 supports trophoblast function and normal fetal development
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77576-z

Normal placental development is fundamental to fetal outcome, yet the molecular pathways that underpin this process remain poorly defined. Here, the authors identify TRPV2 as an essential regulator of placental development. Loss of TRPV2 disrupts trophoblast differentiation and placental architecture, leading to fetal growth restriction, impaired survival and abnormal fetal development in mice.

item.title: Berry curvature multipoles in Kagome superconductor CsV<sub>3</sub>Sb<sub>5</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77618-6

Higher-order nonlinear Hall responses can reveal Berry-curvature multipoles associated with electronic nematicity. Here, the authors identify a vortex-enhanced third-order Hall response in CsV3Sb5 and uncover a Berry-curvature quadrupole associated with chiral loop-current order

item.title: ROS-autocatalytic nanoplatform interfering astrocyte-cancer crosstalk and enhancing glioblastoma therapy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77395-2

Mitochondrial transfer from astrocytes to cancer cells fuels metabolic reprogramming and enhances glioblastoma (GBM) tumorigenicity. Here this group reports a polymeric nanoplatform co-loading S-Gboxin and Galunisertib targeting GBM mitochondria and mitochondrial transfer in astrocyte-cancer cell crosstalk, thereby enhancing GBM therapeutic efficacy.

item.title: Autonomous robotic operation controlled by wave-based neuromorphic hardware
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77661-3

The authors demonstrate autonomous robotic control using wave-based neuromorphic hardware. Physical wave interference performs reservoir computing for obstacle recognition and real-time robot navigation, with a route toward solid-state implementations based on spin waves.

item.title: Spontaneous formation of picoliter water bridges
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77515-y

Water evaporation at the microscale is primarily governed by vapor diffusion and capillarity, but the stability of picoliter water bridges remained poorly explained. Here, the authors demonstrate that adsorption at solid interfaces can significantly inhibit evaporation, thereby enabling the spontaneous formation and long-term stability of picoliter water bridges through an energy-minimization mechanism, as visualized by X-ray imaging.

item.title: Visible light suppresses carbon formation on Ni/CeO<sub>2</sub> catalyst in methane dry reforming reaction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77706-7

Carbon deposition hampers the conversion of methane and carbon dioxide into syngas. Here, the authors use visible light to help oxygen move through a nickel-based catalyst, preventing carbon deposits while boosting methane conversion and hydrogen production.

item.title: End processing in NHEJ by Polymerase λ and PNKP is coordinated during short-range synapsis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77503-2

Non-homologous end joining restores damaged DNA ends through a variety of enzymes that fill gaps, chemically cleanup termini, and ultimately ligate the DNA. Here, the authors show that the end-processing factors Pol λ and PNKP coordinate their activities with LigIV during short-range synapsis.

item.title: An elite allele TaNPF7.6-A1mod enhances nitrogen use efficiency and grain yield in wheat
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76836-2

Improving nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is a key objective in wheat breeding. Here, the authors identify a superior allele, TaNPF7.6-A1mod, and its upstream regulatory factors, demonstrating their roles in enhancing NUE and increasing grain yield in wheat.

item.title: Genome-directed discovery of an octalin-containing polyether ionophore improves diabetic skin wound healing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77444-w

Chronic skin wounds in diabetes mellitus pose a clinical challenge that requires additional therapeutics. Here the authors report a polyether biosynthetic gene cluster, engineer a bioproduction platform for the ionophore polydecalinmycin, and demonstrate its wound healing abilities.

item.title: Author Correction: Engineering immunomodulatory and osteoinductive implant surfaces via mussel adhesion-mediated ion coordination and molecular clicking
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77695-7

Author Correction: Engineering immunomodulatory and osteoinductive implant surfaces via mussel adhesion-mediated ion coordination and molecular clicking

item.title: Explainable data generation from observed small samples by matrix tri-factorization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77343-0

Here the authors propose an explainable data generation approach called EDG that operates under extreme sample scarcity by exploiting inherent low-dimensional principles contained in the observed high-dimensional data via matrix tri-factorization.

item.title: A nested case-control study of air pollution and congenital heart defects via circulating proteins
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77623-9

Prenatal exposure to air pollution has been linked to risk of congenital heart defects (CHD). Here the authors report that periconception exposure, especially to NO₂, is associated with higher CHD risk and distinct maternal and cord blood protein signatures.

item.title: Repeatable, low-drift recordings in behaving nonhuman primates using flexible microelectrodes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77421-3

Stable single-neuron recordings are essential for understanding brain function and enabling future neurotechnologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that flexible polymer microelectrodes provide repeatable recordings in awake nonhuman primates with comparable yield and reduced electrode drift.

item.title: A topographic protomap in mouse subplate neurons precedes the onset of sensory experience
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77454-8

The authors find that subplate neurons receive organized eye- and ear-driven activity before sensory experience and maturation of layer 4 inputs in mice. They persist, receive thalamic inputs, and retain tonotopic responses, suggesting a role in sensory computation.

item.title: Pervasive weak incompatibilities shape phenotypic variation and genome evolution in yeast hybrids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77469-1

Species barriers maintain co-adapted genomes, while interspecific hybridization creates divergent mosaic genomes with uncertain evolutionary potential. This study uses recombinant yeast hybrids to reveal widespread weak interactions and distinct, background-dependent paths of adaptation.

item.title: A cytoskeleton-associated Plasmodium protein critical for organelle segregation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77586-x

The Plasmodium cytoskeleton is critical for parasite replication. Here, Navarro et al identify and characterise a cytoskeleton-associated protein required for organelle segregation and asexual replication.

item.title: Symmetry-cooperative optical-field engineering for ultrabroadband bulk photovoltaic photodetection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77486-0

The authors establish device‑scale optical‑field symmetry asa powerful design degree of freedom for extending bulk photovoltaic photodetection into low‑energy spectral regimes atroom temperature.

item.title: Interface-induced tensile strain stabilizes ruthenium oxide for high-performance acidic water oxidation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77521-0

Ruthenium oxide can lower the demand for scarce iridium in acidic water electrolysis, but its long-term stability is limited. Here, the authors report a two-dimensional carbon-ruthenium oxide composite that stabilizes active sites and enables durable water-splitting performance.

item.title: Deep learning CT signature for predicting early liver metastases in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77665-z

Predicting the risk of early liver micrometastases (ELM) is crucial for identifying patients who are most likely to benefit from neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) yet most deep learning models focus mainly on primary tumours. Here, the authors show that the non-invasive Mamba based model is able to integrate multi-phase spatiotemporal CT imaging features from both the primary pancreatic tumour and liver regions to predict the risk of ELM in PDAC.

item.title: Ferroelectrically programmable lanthanide luminescent memristor
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77397-0

Spatial-light computing is limited by the lack of compact, non-volatile, rewritable analog devices. Wen et al. report a ferroelectric crystal that converts lanthanide emission into a rewritable, multilevel memory, allowing stored optical states to be read and used as persistent weights for neuromorphic computing.

item.title: On-chip 3D printing of metal microinductors for radio frequency electronics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77493-1

Researchers use precision electrodeposition to 3D print copper microinductors directly onto chip contact pads. By extending above the chip surface, the coils decouple inductance from planar silicon area while maintaining inductive operation up to 15 GHz.

item.title: Temporal prediction captures retinal spiking responses across animal species
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77399-y

Functional roles of retina in visual processing are not fully understood. This paper shows that a spiking neural network model trained to efficiently predict future visual input captures many features of retinal activity and does so better than one trained to efficiently encode only the current visual input.

item.title: Contact percolation governs collective motility via mechano-chemical feedback in heterogeneous breast cancer
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77357-8

Percolation describes how network components become progressively more interconnected until they form a connected cluster. Here, the authors discover that contact percolation controls motility and phenotype switching in heterogenous populations of breast cancer cells.

item.title: Ki-67 regulates heterochromatin organization in neurons and forms condensates with heterochromatic components
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77430-2

Chromatin organisation is critical for neuronal function, and its disruption is linked to neurodevelopmental disease. Here, the authors show that Ki‑67 regulates heterochromatin compartment organisation and promotes HP1α-chromatin condensation, implicating phase separation in both normal neurodevelopment and ANAPC7 syndrome.

item.title: Precision inflammation targeting via myeloperoxidase mediated antioxidant melanin nanomedicines for chronic inflammation therapy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77133-8

Chronic inflammation threats health due to unspecific drugs. Here the authors show in hepatopulmonary syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease models, an anti-inflammatory melanin nanomedicine platform that targets inflamed tissues and is mediated by myeloperoxidase.

item.title: Acoustic topological Jackiw–Rebbi states at symmetry broken interfaces
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77579-w

Topological interface states usually rely on explicit symmetry breaking. Here, authors show that spontaneous symmetry breaking at an acoustic metagrating interface generates topological Jackiw-Rebbi states, enabling robust, highly directional sound radiation.

item.title: Periodic polar vortices in BaTiO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> superlattices monolithically grown on silicon
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 08 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77270-0

The authors present the stabilization of polar vortex tubes in epitaxial BaTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices monolithically grown on silicon, and their temperature behavior. Phase field simulations give insight into the strain-dependent evolution of the polar domains.

item.title: Harvesting environmental circadian oscillations for energy autonomy of soft robots
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77422-2

Researchers developed a soft robotic system that harvests energy from naturally occurring thermal oscillations, enabling electronics-free robots to move autonomously without external power or repeated manual recharging.

item.title: Superior flexibility merges high power density in single-crystal Bi<sub>2</sub>Te<sub>3</sub> film thermoelectric generators
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77574-1

This work demonstrates an antisite-defect suppression strategy for Bi2Te3 single-crystal thin films, enabling flexible thermoelectric generators that deliver high power output and long-term bending durability for wearable microelectronic applications.

item.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of tire wear particles reveal escalating emission inequalities across China’s road network
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77475-3

As vehicle exhaust emissions fall, tire and road wear particles (TRWP) are becoming a major PM2.5 source. In China, road traffic emitted 425 kt of TRWP PM2.5 in 2023, concentrating risks in cities. Without action, TRWP will grow by 2050, but targeted measures could cut emissions by 41%.

item.title: SPE-55 and VHA-18 are essential for FB-MO complex assembly and transport during spermatogenesis in C. elegans
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75577-6

This study shows that SPE-55 and VHA-18 coordinate fibrous body–membranous organelle assembly during C. elegans spermatogenesis, providing a mechanism for how sperm cargoes are sorted and directionally transported.

item.title: Plasmid–Host Networks Reveal Persistent Mobile Elements Across Wastewater Treatment
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77447-7

Using Hi-C metagenomics, this study maps how plasmids associate with bacterial hosts across wastewater treatment. They find that plasmid host range narrows from influent to effluent, and a few bacterial families act as persistent plasmid reservoir.

item.title: Telomere variant sequences encode the genetic blueprint for allele-specific telomere length
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77310-9

The authors use long-read sequencing to map allele-specific telomere lengths and telomere variant sequences (TVS). They find that TVSs dispersed along the telomere repeat region are heritable genetic elements that account for the extreme heterogeneity of telomere length between alleles.

item.title: Extreme-bandwidth valley photonic metamaterials approaching Dirac velocity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77577-y

The authors demonstrate ultrabroadband valley transport with near-Dirac group velocity through Dirac-mass engineering and mode control.

item.title: Glucose-induced histone lactylation confers metformin resistance in colorectal cancer stem cells
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77051-9

Metformin has been proposed as a therapy for cancer, but many reports are showing limited efficacy. Here, the authors show that in high-glucose conditions, histone lactylation induces fatty acid uptake leading to metformin resistance in colorectal cancer stem cells.

item.title: PRMT7 restricts CD8+ T cells expansion via the NF-ΚB pathway
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77155-2

Cytotoxic T cells (CTL) are successfully employed in tumour therapy but understanding how their expansion and effector function is regulated might result in further improvements. Here the authors show by a T-cell-specific deletion of Prmt7 and by developing a PRMT7-targeting PROTAC degrader that PRMT7 is a negative regulator of the NF-κB pathway in CTL, removing of which improves anti-tumour function of CTL.

item.title: Optical excitation of nonreciprocal antiferromagnetic magnons at sub-terahertz frequencies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77570-5

The authors demonstrate that optically excited subterahertz magnons in canted antiferromagnetic hematite propagate nonreciprocally at high group velocities, offering potential for ultrafast spintronic applications.

item.title: Steric control of signaling bias in the immunometabolic receptor GPR84
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77312-7

This study reveals how subtle changes in ligand structure control signaling bias at the immunometabolic receptor GPR84, providing structural details for the rational design of drugs with tailored signalling properties.

item.title: OXR1 is a dual redox–mitochondrial checkpoint governing osteoclast differentiation and bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77379-2

Osteoclasts need to manage reactive oxygen species by coordinating redox control and mitochondrial quality maintenance. Here, the authors identify OXR1 as a regulator of osteoclastogenesis and mitophagy, and show that genetic or pharmacological targeting of OXR1 attenuates bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model.

item.title: Selectively intraparticle oxygen dissociation and metalloid mineralization for long-term groundwater remediation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77247-z

Toxic arsenic, antimony and selenium in groundwater are mineralized inside lattice-modified iron nanoparticles with a 98-fold greater stability during long-term aging in groundwater, offering an economic in-situ remediation strategy.

item.title: Whole genome sequencing of 1427 Mexican individuals from the oriGen cohort
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77389-0

Mexican populations remain underrepresented in genomics. Here, Aguilar-Ordoñez et al. report on 1,481 whole-genomes from the oriGen project, identifying key variants like a CNV driving the Rh-negative blood group.

item.title: Interfacial engineering strategies and sustainability assessment for direct electrolysis of dilute CO<sub>2</sub> streams
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77516-x

Direct electrochemical upgrading of dilute CO2 from flue gas is attractive but limited by poor local CO2 availability and selectivity. Here, the authors report interfacial engineering strategies to enrich local CO2 and improve selectivity, supported by technoeconomic and life-cycle assessments.

item.title: All-electrical magnetisation switching via tilting spin propagation and polarization in MnTe spin source
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77568-z

This work proposes a novel approach to achieve all-electrical magnetization switching by tilting the crystal structure of the spin source material, thereby manipulating the spin transport and polarization direction.

item.title: A divergent betacoronavirus with a functional furin cleavage site in South American bats
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77599-6

There is still limited data reported on virus diversity in South American bats. In this study, the authors report a divergent betacoronavirus with a functional furin cleavage site in South American bats, expanding knowledge of coronavirus diversity and features linked to zoonotic potential.

item.title: Unconditional and exponentially large violation of classicality
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77413-3

The authors introduce a practical game that distinguishes quantum from classical behaviour without relying on unproven assumptions. Quantum computers achieve exponentially larger scores than any classical strategy, a result confirmed in experiments.

item.title: Dysregulated tissue immunity in human fatal asthma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77256-y

Immune mechanisms driving severe asthma and fatal outcomes remain elusive. Through cross-tissue immune profiling of organ donors who died of fatal asthma versus other causes, the authors here reveal mucosal immune dysregulation marked by enhanced T- and B-cell memory, reduced Tregs, and increased lung Th2 and Th1 effectors linked to priming in gut-associated lymph nodes.

item.title: Thermal conductivity predictions with foundation atomistic models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76391-w

Researchers show how foundation atomistic models can predict heat transport and thermal expansion, using physics-based benchmarks and fine-tuning to reach first-principles accuracy.

item.title: Global lake tipping vulnerability under sustained agricultural exposure
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77445-9

Lakes tip into degraded states mainly because of what already surrounds them, not new developments. Chronic agricultural exposure and baseline water quality globally predict abrupt shifts better than early warning signals.

item.title: Author Correction: Unequal exchange of labour in the world economy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77488-y

Author Correction: Unequal exchange of labour in the world economy

item.title: Twinned-magnesium metal negative electrodes enable reversible magnesium electrodeposition
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77543-8

Twin boundaries in magnesium can enable fast charging. Here, the authors engineer these crystal defects to guide metal growth, enabling stable cycling at 30 mA cm-2. This design allows for rapid plating and stripping, paving the way for high-power batteries that charge in minutes.

item.title: Toward efficient green methanol from biomass and renewable power
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77364-9

The study compares four routes for producing green methanol from biomass and renewable power, revealing trade-offs in carbon use, energy efficiency, emissions and cost, and identifying the deployment boundaries for each route.

item.title: Unified down-stream analysis of crosslinking mass spectrometry results with pyXLMS
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77407-1

Crosslinking mass spectrometry (XLMS) has become the method of choice for uncovering protein interactions and structure in vivo. Here, the authors present pyXLMS – a python package and web application – to streamline the down-stream analysis of XLMS results to extract biological meaning.

item.title: Probing electron transport and thermodynamic properties in expanded warm dense matter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77435-x

Despite the ubiquity of warm dense matter states, there is lack of well-established models describing the expanded regime. To address this gap, the authors provide theoretical and experimental analysis of warm dense aluminium by means of pulse Joule heating. This provides constraints to the equation of state and insight into the electrical conductivity behaviour.

item.title: Ubiquity and seasonality of deep submesoscales in the Southern Ocean revealed by elephant seals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77299-1

Instrumented elephant seals reveal that deep submesoscale motions are a ubiquitous and seasonally varying component of Southern Ocean circulation, with their intensity below the mixed layer closely tracking mesoscale eddy activity and supporting an eddy-driven origin.

item.title: Entropy engineering for advanced microwave ceramics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77398-z

Entropy engineering, as a design strategy, regulates oxygen octahedral geometry to optimizedielectric constant, quality factor, and thermal stability. The authors fabricate a dielectric antenna, demonstrating the potential applications.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Socio-economic value of data-driven eruption forecasts to balance false alarms against catastrophic loss
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Perceived humanness and empathy are dissociated in relationship advice generated by a large language model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77350-1

Large language models can generate empathic language similar to human writing. The authors show that empathic language and perceived humanness are dissociated, revealing stochastic empathy in AI systems.

item.title: Author Correction: A multicellular self-organized probiotic platform for oral delivery enhances intestinal colonization
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76863-z

Author Correction: A multicellular self-organized probiotic platform for oral delivery enhances intestinal colonization

item.title: Author Correction: Machine learning model-guided selective use of temporary diverting ileostomy in rectal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77496-y

Author Correction: Machine learning model-guided selective use of temporary diverting ileostomy in rectal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial

item.title: Paleogeographic controls on Phanerozoic weathering rates and implications for climate regulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77289-3

Simulations with randomized continents show that temperature- and hydrology-controlled weathering results in climates that track different features of continental geometry. The Earth’s record suggests the control may have shifted over 480 million years.

item.title: Author Correction: High expression of Rex-orf-I and HBZ mRNAs and bronchiectasis in lung of HTLV-1A/C infected macaques
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77329-y

Author Correction: High expression of Rex-orf-I and HBZ mRNAs and bronchiectasis in lung of HTLV-1A/C infected macaques

item.title: Author Correction: Double-stranded RNA and ROS scavenging nanoplatform for modulating skin inflammation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77494-0

Author Correction: Double-stranded RNA and ROS scavenging nanoplatform for modulating skin inflammation

item.title: Heterogeneity in the response to the metabolic environment drives fosfomycin heteroresistance
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77232-6

Choby et al. show an antibiotic-resistant subpopulation is generated by heterogeneity in expression of an antibiotic importer repressed by environmental glucose, suggesting diabetes-related infection environments may influence antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Ultra-low-power probabilistic graphical computing based on memristors enabling communications signal processing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77169-w

To address the energy bottleneck in modern mobile communications, Jiang et al. introduce a memristor-based framework unifying key wireless signal-processing tasks. It achieves sub-10 pJ/bit consumption and an 11.4-fold efficiency gain while maintaining low error rates for edge communications.

item.title: Drought development characteristics modulate global dry–wet abrupt alternation through distinct land–atmosphere feedbacks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77272-y

The study finds that nearly one-third of droughts worldwide are followed by extreme precipitation, with drought-development characteristics distinguishing distinct pathways to these dry–wet transitions.

item.title: Ten critical questions for scaling up floating developments
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77492-2

Floating developments may offer climate-adaptive solutions to space scarcity and water management challenges in coastal, inland, and offshore contexts. We present ten research questions to explore the potential for safe, inclusive, sustainable and economically viable upscaling towards large-scale floating developments.

item.title: Unsupervised discovery of functional sequence patterns from protein language model with MotifAE
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77333-2

Protein language models (pLMs) capture biologically meaningful sequence patterns, but the features learned by these models remain largely opaque. Here the authors present MotifAE, an interpretable sparse autoencoder framework that reveals diverse sequence motifs and structural domains from pLM embeddings, improves recovery of known functional motifs and identifies features linked to domain function and folding stability, enabling stability-specific fitness landscape prediction.

item.title: Unveiling hidden air pollution exposure and impacts with low-cost sensor network-based frameworks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77148-1

This study integrates dense, low-cost sensor-based PM2.5 measurements with machine learning models, recent family health survey data, and India-specific relative risk information to assess sub-regional exposure inequity among socioeconomic groups and short-term mortality impacts in Bihar, one of the most polluted and understudied states of India.

item.title: Observation of a spin-textured nematic Kondo lattice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74841-z

The authors study the layered Kondo magnet USbTe by spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy. They discover a spin-polarized nematic state below 15 K, coinciding with the formation of heavy quasi-particles driven by band hybridization.

item.title: Sex- and fiber type-specific remodeling of the muscle proteome implicates CSRP3 in resistance training-induced hypertrophy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77275-9

Here, the authors show that changes in the muscle fiber proteome following 8 weeks of resistance training are both sex- and fiber type-specific. This includes greater upregulation of CSRP3 in type II than type I fibers, which in mice was shown to be involved in muscle growth.

item.title: Selective organ deposition of nanoparticles directed by metal–organic network coatings
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77181-0

Developing a simple and broadly applicable strategy for tailoring the organ tropism of nanoparticles has been a long-standing challenge. Here, the authors address this challenge by introducing a metal–organic network coating approach that enables selective organ tropism across a wide range of established nanoparticle platforms by varying the coating composition.

item.title: Macrocyclization of native peptides through (thio)urea crosslinking of two amines
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77301-w

Cyclopeptides are promising candidates for developing bioactive molecules and drugs, but due to the scarcity of efficient cyclization strategies for natural peptides, the development of novel cyclopeptides remains challenging. Here, the authors report the development of a variety of macrocyclic peptides featuring (thio)urea bridges through site-selective Lys-Lys crosslinking of native peptides, employing N,N′-carbonyldiimidazole (CDI) or N,N′- thiocarbonyldiimidazole (TCDI) as bridging reagents.

item.title: DNA methylation either antagonizes or promotes Polycomb recruitment at transposable elements in Arabidopsis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77108-9

Here the authors show that in Arabidopsis, DNA methylation can both antagonize and promote Polycomb silencing in a direct, locus-specific manner, thus revealing an interplay that shapes the epigenome.

item.title: Common alleles associated with connectivity within and across the brain’s main functional networks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77476-2

This study identified 114 independent SNPs (315 candidate genes) associated with brain’s functional connectivity, showing a large genetic commonality affecting connectivity across different brain networks and with several neuropsychiatric conditions.

item.title: Disentangling cation–polyanion coupling reveals which anion motion dominates cation transport in solid electrolytes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77273-x

Fast ion transport in solid electrolytes is often attributed to anion rotation. Simulations of six materials show that rotation, translation or vibration can dominate transport, depending on how rapidly anions reorient relative to cation hopping.

item.title: Photon-driven magnetization switching in Fe₃GeTe₂ enables programmable, multilevel magnetic memory
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77178-9

This work demonstrates that pulsed optical excitation enables reversible all-optical switching of the magnetic state in Fe₃GeTe₂ and reveals the roles of photon energy, fluence, and polarization in governing the switching behavior

item.title: A spin-photon interface in the telecom C-band with long hole spin dephasing time
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77282-w

Spin-photon interfaces based on telecom wavelength quantum dots require long-lived spin qubits for quantum networking applications. Here, the authors demonstrate a hole spin dephasing time exceeding 20 ns in a telecom band quantum dot integrated in a circular Bragg grating, setting a new benchmark for spin coherence in this platform.

item.title: Trifluoroacetate mediated reduction of atherosclerosis in mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77341-2

Trifluoroacetate (TFA), long assumed to be an inert peptide counterion, is a bioactive modulator of PPARα signaling that induces peroxisome proliferation, alters lipid metabolism, and attenuates atherosclerosis in mice.

item.title: Author Correction: Concavity-enhanced chiral self-assembly of anisotropic nanoparticles toward strong chiroptical activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77323-4

Author Correction: Concavity-enhanced chiral self-assembly of anisotropic nanoparticles toward strong chiroptical activity

item.title: Quinone-heme π-π interactions bridge the biotic-abiotic interface for enhanced methanogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77276-8

Quinone-based conductive materials promote extracellular electron transfer and methanogenesis during anaerobic digestion, in which the material mediates the transfer of electrons produced from exoelectrogens to electrotrophic methanogens, but the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Here, the authors establish the electron transfer interface between reduced anthraquinone (H₂AQC) and Methanosarcina barkeri in a microbial electrolysis cell, and reveal an intrinsic electronic complementarity between the electron donating π-system of H₂AQC and the electron-accepting iron-porphyrin ring of labile heme b.

item.title: A machine learning method for calculating highly localized protein stabilities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75590-9

PFNet is a machine learning model that infers residue-level protein stabilities from conventional hydrogen exchange-mass spectrometry data, transforming a widely used structural biology technique into a scalable tool for quantitative protein ensemble analysis.

item.title: Ultrathin nano-layered boron nitride stabilizing perovskite quantum dot-based light-emitting diodes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77166-z

Perovskite quantum dot light-emitting diodes are promising for lighting and displays, but poor operational stability limits their use. Wang et al. added an ultrathin boron nitride interlayer to suppress defects, ion migration, and heat sensitivity, improving efficiency and lifetime.

item.title: Lyapunov exponents explain disorder-induced polarization and soliton jumping in a mechanical Markov system
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77157-0

Disordered mechanical systems can exhibit complex properties that are difficult to analyse. Here, the authors introduce a space-time mapping between one-dimensional mechanical systems and discrete-time dynamical systems to reveal disorder-induced polarization, nonuniform soliton transport, and other phenomena.

item.title: Antichiral hinge states in a higher-order photonic nodal ring semimetal
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77020-2

The authors demonstrate antichiral hinge states in a photonic nodal-ring semimetal, revealing co-propagating one-way transport linking bulk, surface and hinge topology, robust to metallic obstacles and reconfigurable by layer addition or removal.

item.title: Coulombic surface dipole trapping ionomer for efficient proton exchange membrane fuel cells
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74391-4

Low-platinum fuel cells need catalyst layers that move protons and oxygen efficiently, but uneven ionomer placement limits performance. Here, the authors report a cobalt single-atom dipole coating which guides the ionomer, protects platinum surfaces and boosts power and durability.

item.title: Efficacy of everolimus and letrozole with or without ribociclib in recurrent endometrial cancer: a phase 2 randomized clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77049-3

Therapeutic options for recurrent endometrial cancer (rEC) are limited. Here, the authors present a randomized phase 2 clinical trial comparing the combination of mTOR and aromatase inhibitors (everolimus and letrozole) with or without the CDK4/6 inhibitor, ribociclib, in patients with rEC.

item.title: Multi-modal learning with incomplete data
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77212-w

Incomplete multi-modal datasets pose a major challenge for real-world machine learning applications. Here, authors present iMML, a unified open-source Python package designed to analyze and integrate incomplete multi-modal datasets for diverse machine learning tasks.

item.title: Grain boundary segregation of ceramic aerogels for reliable thermal insulation at extreme conditions
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77371-w

Grain-boundary segregation enables ceramic aerogels with high thermal stability and reliable thermal insulation at temperatures up to 1500 °C, offering a strategy for designing lightweight thermal protection materials for extreme environments.

item.title: Multidisciplinary intervention in frail elderly patients with cardiovascular diseases: a multicentre, single-blinded, randomised controlled trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77277-7

A hospital-initiated multidisciplinary program was associated with improved frailty and physical function and lower readmission risk in frail elderly patients with cardiovascular diseases, although larger studies are needed to confirm these.

item.title: RBP-Driven RNA sorting and local translation establish the molecular identities of individual sensory axons
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77192-x

Here authors define compartment-specific translatomes in somatosensory dorsal root ganglion neurons and identify distinct local translational programs across central axons, peripheral axons and neuronal somata. They show that the RNA-binding proteins SFPQ and SRSF10 coordinate the selective trafficking and local translation of mRNAs in peripheral and central axons.

item.title: Listeria promotes systemic infection by targeting the host deubiquitinase CYLD
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77063-5

Secretion of protein InlC into the host cytosol is important for virulence of the intracellular pathogen Listeria monocytogenes. Here, Ammendolia et al. show that InlC recruits a host deubiquitinase to cytosolic bacteria in response to ubiquitin-mediated defenses.

item.title: Perirenal fat β₃-adrenergic signaling alleviates renal fibrosis via regulating Bcat2/BCAA-TNFα pathway in diabetic kidney disease
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77325-2

The authors identify perirenal fat ADRB3 signaling as a regulator of diabetic kidney fibrosis through a Bcat2/BCAA-TNFα pathway, suggesting adipose-kidney crosstalk as a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: Predicting ionic conductivity of sulfide glass solid-state electrolytes using max-flow methodology
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77363-w

Here authors present a max-flow method that uses static glass structures to predict how fast ions move, especially in sulfide glasses, helping to accelerate the discovery of high-performance electrolyte materials for batteries.

item.title: Chromosome-level Streptochaeta genome elucidates the ancestral karyotype and allopolyploid origin of grasses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76979-2

Early genomic and karyotypic evolution that underpinned grasses (Poaceae) diversification remains incompletely resolved. Here, the authors report genome assembly of Streptochaeta spicata and reveal the ancestral karyotype, subgenome dominance following genome duplication, and the origin of spikelet.

item.title: Unassisted bipolar photoelectrochemical synthesis of H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75533-4

PEC H2O2 production usually suffers from low selectivity and poor stability. This study shows a Zn-TiO2/BVO/WO3∥Ru:CuO/Nb-CBO bipolar system that enables efficient and stable H2O2 synthesis under sunlight, achieving a combined Faradaic efficiency of 163.37%.

item.title: IFN-γ-driven iNOS induction in macrophages mediates CAR T cell resistance in B cell lymphoma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76972-9

Tumor associated macrophages can support cancer progression by suppressing T cell effector functions. Here the authors report that induction of iNOS in tumor-associated macrophages by IFN-gamma secreted from CAR T cells contributes to the development of CAR-T resistance in B cell lymphoma.

item.title: Mutation-agnostic base editing of the progerin farnesylation site rescues Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome phenotypes in neuromuscular organoids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77251-3

A mutation-agnostic base-editing strategy targeting the LMNA farnesylation site restores DNA repair and nuclear architecture in human progeria neuromuscular organoids and supports transient mRNA-based therapeutic genome editing.

item.title: Dietary protein governs the role of insulin signaling in the postprandial regulation of hepatic mTORC1
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77216-6

The nutrient-sensing kinase complex mTORC1 regulates metabolism, yet the physiological signals controlling its activity in the liver are incompletely defined. Here, the authors show that dietary protein is required for postprandial hepatic mTORC1 activation and determines its responsiveness to insulin.

item.title: OsIDD7 integrates signaling networks for arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77162-3

Here the authors identify IDD7 as a regulator of arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis in rice. They reveal how IDD7 coordinates transcriptional networks that promote beneficial interactions between rice roots and mycorrhizal fungi.

item.title: What one sees depends on how far the eye has moved
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76503-6

People explore the visual world through rapid eye movements called saccades. Here, the authors show that the size of each saccade determines which level of spatial detail becomes most visible after the movement.

item.title: Woven dECM yarn scaffolds enable volumetric muscle loss regeneration via immunomodulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77032-y

Volumetric muscle loss remains a significant unmet clinical need. Herein, the authors report a yarn scaffold based on decellularized extracellular matrix fabricated via 3D weaving of rotary-cut yarns, which achieves precise structural control, full interconnectivity, and high porosity.

item.title: Gut microbiota-activated PLCγ2 monocytes drive atrial fibrillation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77219-3

Atrial fibrillation involves systemic inflammatory activation that remodel the atrial endocardium. Here, the authors show that gut microbiota activate PLCy2 positive monocytes, promoting endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and atrial fibrillation through a microbiota–monocyte–endocardial axis.

item.title: The shifting landscape of brain-wide myelination across the human lifespan
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77073-3

This study presents the development and aging principles of myelination in 214 brain regions using large-scale dataset spanning birth through 100 years. The results provide strong evidence for region-specific variability in multiscale brain development, with some areas exhibiting earlier maturation in myelination and others in macrostructural properties.

item.title: Nanofibrous aerogels with continuous conductivity gradient for ultrabroadband absorption-dominant electromagnetic interference shielding
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77257-x

Electromagnetic interference shields can be limited by impedance mismatch with free space, leading to strong reflections and secondary radiation. Here, the authors introduce lightweight all-polymer aerogels with a continuous through-thickness conductivity gradient, fabricated in a single step via diffusion-driven oxidative polymerization of pyrrole within aramid-nanofiber scaffolds.

item.title: Programmable mesoporous carbon architectures from liquefied wood via reactive-emulsion-mediated self-assembly
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77269-7

Developing biomass-derived self-assembly systems for controlling carbon morphology remains challenging because of their intrinsic heterogeneity, which hinders controllable assembly. Here, the authors report a biomass-enabled reactive-emulsion-mediated strategy for converting liquefied wood into various mesoporous carbon nanomaterials.

item.title: Injury-transduced oligodendrocytes modulate neuroinflammation and glial activation in diseased and non-diseased central nervous system
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76159-2

This study identifies SerpinOLs, injury-responsive oligodendrocytes producing SERPINA3N, as a common cell state in disease and aging, which amplify neuroinflammation and glial activation beyond myelin-related functions in mice.

item.title: Plasmonic-enhanced lanthanide nanotransducers for mid-infrared detection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76701-2

Lanthanide nanotransducers can convert mid-infrared light into nearinfrared signals but suffer from weak emission. Here, authors couple Nd3 + /Yb3 + -doped nanoparticles with gold nanospheres to achieve silicon-readable detection with seven-fold improvement in specific detectivity relative to the pristine nanoparticles.

item.title: Strong and crack-tolerant elastomers via geometrically confined H-bonding semicarbazides
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77193-w

The development of high-performance elastomers that are strong, crack-tolerant, and wear-resistant remains a challenge. Here the authors design a poly(urethane-urea) system based on geometrically confined semicarbazide chain extenders, which enhance the mechanical performance of the material.

item.title: Many-body interactions resolve halide distribution at the air/water interface
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77205-9

How halide ions distribute at the surface of water has long been debated. Here, the authors show that cooperative molecular interactions suppress adsorption, leaving only iodide with a weak surface preference.

item.title: Hydrogen Bond-Enabled Carbon Dot-Based Network for Efficient Inverted Organic Solar Cells with Prolonged Photoelectrical-Mechanical-Moist Stability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76944-z

Long-lasting organic solar cells require transport layers stable in electrical, mechanical and chemical aspects. Cui et al. fabricated a fluorinated carbon dot/polymer electron transport layer, which delivers high efficiency together with excellent humidity and bending stability.

item.title: Persistent chromatin alterations and gene expression reprogramming follow widespread DNA damage in glioblastoma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77331-4

How DNA damage reshapes cancer cells beyond genetic mutations is poorly understood. Here, the authors show that DNA double-strand breaks in glioblastoma cells trigger lasting non-genetic changes in 3D genome folding, gene expression and DNA modifications that persist for weeks.

item.title: Hybrid exosomal nanomotors convert pathological ROS into transport-driving cues to enhance cartilage accumulation in osteoarthritis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76949-8

Osteoarthritis therapies are limited by poor drug transport within dense cartilage. Here, authors develop hybrid exosomal nanomotors that convert pathological ROS into transport-driving cues, enhancing transport within cartilage and slowing osteoarthritis progression.

item.title: Cascade electrosynthesis of glycolic acid from ethylene and oxygen with an energy efficiency of 62.9%
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75221-3

The industrial implementation of ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) to glycolic acid (GA) brings promise but poses a challenge for ethylene cost. Here, the authors report an ORR-ethylene oxidation-EGOR cascade conversion strategy that can boost both energy efficiency and economic viability.

item.title: Unraveling single-molecule reactions via multiplexed in-situ DNA sequencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 29 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77308-3

The authors develop SPIN-Seq, a method that directly links the sequence of individual DNA molecules to their functional behavior, revealing how DNA sequence impacts protein-DNA interactions and the kinetics of biological reactions on nucleic acids.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Combinatorial group testing for efficient scaling across biological applications
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: The Labrador Sea as a conduit for AMOC lower-limb transport anomalies on multiple timescales
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77271-z

The study shows that, despite the Labrador Sea forming the final leg of the Atlantic overturning circulation’s subpolar ‘relay’, transport changes originating in the Irminger and Iceland basins exert the strongest downstream influence.

item.title: Cell-inspired dual-tandem catalytic nanoreactors drive targeted hearing protection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76994-3

Here, the authors present a biomimetic nanoreactor that mimics natural antioxidant enzymes, rebuilds cochlear redox homeostasis and protects against noise‑induced hearing loss by preserving hair cells and synaptic function.

item.title: A programmable lipid-triggered allosteric site modulates LC3 LIR receptor binding activity
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76697-9

The allosteric mechanisms by which lipid binding controls protein activity remain poorly understood. Here, the authors identify a lipid-triggered allosteric site in LC3 that remodels its receptor-binding interface upon membrane interaction. This site can be engineered to precisely tune LC3-LIR interactions, offering a new strategy to regulate selective autophagy.

item.title: Carbon distribution in planet Mercury from magma ocean evolution to graphite crust and core composition
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75458-y

This study investigates how carbon was distributed within Mercury during its formation, using high-pressure, high-temperature experiments to simulate conditions in the planet’s early magma ocean. The results show that Mercury’s unique graphite-rich crust and core composition are linked to extremely reducing conditions, which favored carbon retention in the crust and mantle rather than the core.

item.title: CD97/ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76948-9

Allergic asthma involves different lung cells and mediators. Here, the authors examine the function of CD97/ADGRE5 and show that its absence increases the severity of allergic lung inflammation in mice. Allergen-pulsed Cd97-/- DCs are more activated and promote stronger type 2 immune responses than WT DCs and, in humans, lung DCs from allergen-exposed asthmatics express less CD97 than allergic non-asthmatics.

item.title: Wireless IoT-enabled microneedle electroceutical for personalized and connected pain management
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 28 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76527-y

Skin-attached electrotherapeutic devices suffer from unstable skin-electrode interface. Here, the authors present a thermoresponsive conductive adhesive microneedle electroceutical providing stable, safe stimulation and IoT-based personalized pain therapy with healthcare-provider oversight.

item.title: Quantum nonlinearity for optical neural computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77202-y

Optical neural networks could cut the energy cost of AI, yet weak optical nonlinearity limits their capability. Here, the authors propose activation units by embedding a quantum emitter in an inverse-designed photonic structure, numerically demonstrating all-optical deep learning at nanowatt-scale intensities.

item.title: 3D printed designer color routers with low refractive index for low-light imaging
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76072-8

The authors demonstrate a 3D-printed low-refractive-index color router that replaces absorptive color filters, improving light collection and enabling brighter, more efficient color imaging under both normal and low-light conditions.

item.title: The endo-lysosomal system drives lumen formation in a human epiblast model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77140-9

Rengarajan et al. identify RAB35- and RAB7-regulated endo-lysosomal dynamics as important drivers of the formation of the apicosome and lumen formation in a model of human epiblast formation. This study presents new insights into peri-implantation human embryo morphogenesis.

item.title: Automated transition state generation for mechanistic exploration in organic synthesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77230-8

The authors develop UniTS, a unified framework for automated transition state generation that combines a diverse transition state dataset with equivariant diffusion learning to accelerate mechanistic exploration.
